answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that grows slowly: a new agent starts with a thin vine of trust and must earn attestation from established peers before its votes count. Tie each account to a scarce, verifiable resource, like locked collateral or a proven work history, so duplicate identities cost more to maintain than they earn. Like water finding a narrow inlet, sybils can enter but cannot flood the ledger. A velvet-gloved rate limit on new entrants completes the picture.
